extracted.intended_audience: professional research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry/number theory familiar with Frobenioids and Inter-Universal Teichmüller (IUT) theory
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, constructions, and structural properties (existence, uniqueness, compatibilities, symmetries) for ×/×μ-Kummer structures, (split-)Kummer Frobenioids, F-prime-strips and their enhanced (cid:4)×μ-versions arising in IUT theory; includes functorial links (Θ×μ, Θ×μ_gau), invariants and symmetry constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: ×-Kummer and ×μ-Kummer structure (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A ×-Kummer structure (respectively, ×μ-Kummer structure) on a Frobenioid C is a Z×- (respectively, Ism-) orbit of isomorphisms κ× : O×(G) ∼→ O×(A) (respectively κ×μ : O×μ(G) ∼→ O×μ(A)) of ind-topological G-modules, where A is a universal covering pro-object and G = Aut(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording emphasizes these as orbits of isomorphisms of ind-topological G-modules; independence of choice of A follows since universal covers are isomorphic. Any ×-Kummer structure is unique (Remark 1.11.1, (b) referenced). For ×μ, the structure is described in terms of the images I^κ_H(A) for open subgroups H ⊆ G and is equivalent to the collection {I^κ_H(A)}_H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of ×μ-Kummer structure by H-invariant submodules
rubrics_metrics.description: A ×μ-Kummer structure κ×μ on C determines, for each open subgroup H ⊆ G, a submodule I^κ_H(A) := Im(O×(G)^H) ⊆ O×μ(A), and conversely κ×μ is completely determined by the collection of these submodules as H ranges over open subgroups of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tautological identification (Example 1.8, (iv)): the unique Ism-orbit of G-equivariant isomorphisms O×μ(G) ∼→ O×μ(A) maps O×(G)^H onto I^κ_H(A) for each H. Thus to specify a ×μ-Kummer structure it suffices to specify these images for all open H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer Frobenioid / split-Kummer Frobenioid (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A [×-, ×μ-]Kummer Frobenioid is a Frobenioid equipped with a [×-, ×μ-]Kummer structure. A split-[×-, ×μ-]Kummer Frobenioid is a split Frobenioid equipped with such a Kummer structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminology: labelling of Frobenioids equipped with the above Kummer structures; split- prefix denotes split Frobenioids. Uniqueness remarks (for ×-structures) justify certain abuses of notation later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and uniqueness of canonical isomorphisms at bad/good places
rubrics_metrics.description: For the local/profinite groups arising from universal covers (‡G = Aut(‡A)), there exists a unique Z×-orbit of isomorphisms ‡κ×_w : O×(‡G) ∼→ O×(‡A) and an induced Ism-orbit ‡κ×μ_w : O×μ(‡G) ∼→ O×μ(‡A) (Remark and Definition 4.9 (ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from the group-theoretic algorithms G→(G (cid:2) O×(G)) and the uniqueness in Remark 1.11.1, (b). The local canonical isomorphisms are the building blocks for constructing local split-Kummer Frobenioids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of model Frobenioid from O(cid:4)×μ(‡A) and divisor monoid
rubrics_metrics.description: The monoid with ‡G-action O(cid:4)×μ(‡A), together with the divisor monoid of the underlying Frobenioid, determines a 'model Frobenioid' equipped with a splitting; evaluation at ‡A identifies its unit and monoid groups with O×μ(‡A) and O(cid:4)×μ(‡A), and the associated Ism-orbit determines a ×μ-Kummer structure (Definition 4.9 (iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides how to pass from local monoid data and splittings to a model Frobenioid carrying the Kummer structure; justification references [FrdI], Theorem 5.2, (ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inductive-system construction for Varc (archimedean-like) places
rubrics_metrics.description: For v ∈ Varc, replace the split Frobenioid by the inductive system (indexed by cofinal multiplicative subsets of N≥1) of split Frobenioids formed by quotienting by N-torsion; the units of this inductive system give a topological group (noncanonically S1) related via compatible surjections (‡D_v)^× → O×μN(A), yielding a Kummer-type structure reconstructible algorithmically (Definition 4.9 (v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how to handle archimedean/Varc places: form an inductive system of split Frobenioids, identify compatible surjections whose kernels are N-torsion, and interpret this as a Kummer-like structure up to an indeterminacy given by automorphism of (‡D_v)^×.

rubrics_metrics.name: F (cid:3)(cid:5)-prime-strip (local isomorphism condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: An F (cid:3)(cid:5)-prime-strip ∗F = {∗F_v}_v∈V is a collection of data such that for each v ∈ V, ∗F_v is isomorphic to the standard local model ‡F_v (as in Definition 4.9 (vii)). A morphism is a collection of isomorphisms indexed by V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the local-to-global criterion for a prime-strip: each local constituent must match the prescribed canonical local model up to isomorphism; morphisms are pointwise isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: F (cid:3)(cid:4)×μ-prime-strip (global conditions and pilot object)
rubrics_metrics.description: An F (cid:3)(cid:4)×μ-prime-strip is a collection (∗C, Prime(∗C)∼→V, ∗F(cid:3)(cid:4)×μ, {∗ρ_v}_v∈V) satisfying conditions (a)–(f) of IUTchI Definition 5.2 (iv), with the F(cid:3)-portion replaced by the F(cid:3)(cid:4)×μ data; the generators of the monoids O(cid:4)(−) at v∈Vbad together with the {∗ρ_w} determine a pilot object of negative arithmetic degree well-defined up to isomorphism (Definition 4.9 (viii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires fulfillment of the enumerated axioms (a)-(f) from IUTchI; emphasizes that the global pilot object (a realiﬁed Frobenioid of negative arithmetic degree) is produced from the local monoid generators and compatibility data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of Constant Prime-Strips from Ψcns
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying the constructions of Corollary 4.6 (i),(iii) to the underlying Θ±ell-Hodge theater of †HT Θ±ellNF produces, for each label t ∈ LabCusp±(†D), a collection Ψcns(†F)_t which determines an F-prime-strip; identifications via isomorphisms of Corollary 4.6 yield a specific F-prime-strip †F (Corollary 4.10 (i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the recipe for constructing F-prime-strips from the constant-data constructions Ψcns and mandates compatibility with the F±_l-symmetrizing isomorphisms referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theta and Gaussian prime-strip constructions and evaluation isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying Corollary 4.6 (iv),(v) to Θ-bridge and Θ±ell-Hodge theater data produces collections ΨFenv and ΨFgau whose global realiﬁed Frobenioids and local isomorphisms Φ_env,v and Φ_gau,v give rise to F-prime-strips †F_env and †F_gau; the evaluation isomorphisms of Corollary 4.6 (iv),(v) induce an evaluation isomorphism between these F-prime-strips (Corollary 4.10 (ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specifies how to build the environment and Gaussian prime-strips and the canonical evaluation isomorphism relating them; stresses naturality relative to underlying Θ-Hodge theaters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial Θ×μ- and Θ×μ_gau-links (full poly-isomorphism)
rubrics_metrics.description: The functorial algorithm of Definition 4.9 (vi) applied to an F (cid:3)-prime-strip and its associated F (cid:3)(cid:4)×μ-prime-strip induces maps from Isom_F(†F, ‡F) to Isom_F(cid:2)×μ (†F(cid:3)(cid:4)×μ, ‡F(cid:3)(cid:4)×μ), producing a full poly-isomorphism called the Θ×μ-link (and analogously the Θ×μ_gau-link) — a poly-isomorphism between Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters (Corollary 4.10 (iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View these links as functorially lifted isomorphisms between prime-strips to their ×μ-enhanced versions, producing poly-isomorphisms (multi-component isomorphisms) between Hodge theaters; the construction is nonempty and natural.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coricity of F×μ-prime-strips and induced D-Θ±ellNF-link (invariance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural isomorphisms arise between †F(cid:3)×μ and its env/gau variants; composing these with poly-isomorphisms from Θ×μ- and Θ×μ_gau-links yields a full poly-isomorphism which is an invariant of both links and induces an associated D-Θ±ellNF-link between the associated D-prime-strips (Corollary 4.10 (iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'coricity' refers to preservation/canonical identification of the unit (theta) portions; this property yields invariants at the D-prime-strip level and provides the D-link between Hodge theaters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism of global realiﬁed Frobenioid collections compatible with R>0-orbits
rubrics_metrics.description: The full poly-isomorphism of F-prime-strips induces an isomorphism between collections of data (Frobenioid, Prime bijection, collection of topological monoid isomorphisms) which is compatible with the R>0-orbits arising from the natural R>0-actions that scale arithmetic degrees (Corollary 4.10 (v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies compatibility requirement under positive real scalings of arithmetic degrees, referencing [FrdI] for the R>0-actions and indicating that isomorphisms are respected up to these orbits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenius-picture infinite chains and symmetry constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying Θ×μ- and Θ×μ_gau-links to a sequence of distinct Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters produces infinite chains (Frobenius-pictures) that may be represented as an oriented graph Γ admitting a natural Z-translation symmetry but not arbitrary permutation symmetries (e.g., no automorphism switching two adjacent vertices and fixing the rest) (Corollary 4.10 (vi)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a structural/graph-theoretic invariant: the chain has translation symmetry but is order-conscious; prohibits certain local permutations — an essential constraint on allowable automorphisms of the chain/graph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Étale-picture of D-Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters and permutation symmetry of spokes
rubrics_metrics.description: The induced infinite chain of D-linked D-Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters produces an étale-picture where the mono-analytic core (−)D forms a constant invariant and the spokes (distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures) admit arbitrary permutation symmetries among themselves (Corollary 4.11 (i),(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrasts with the Frobenius-picture: the étale-picture is permutation-symmetric among spokes; the mono-analytic core is an invariant (mono-analytic core / constant invariant) of the chain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coricity of units and its role in log-wall/volume comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'coricity of F×μ-prime-strips' amounts to the coricity of D-prime-strips together with coricity of (various torsion quotients of) the units O×(−) of the Frobenioids; this coricity of the units will be central for applying the log-wall theory and for comparing volumes across Θ×μ- and Θ×μ_gau-links (Remark 4.10.3 (i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Underlines a required structural property (coricity of units) that must hold for later analytic comparisons (log-wall applications); treat this as a necessary invariant/compatibility condition when constructing or evaluating these objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-preservation of value-group/divisor-monoid under links (Teichmüller deformation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The value-group (divisor-monoid) portion of the Frobenioids is in general not preserved by the Θ×μ- and Θ×μ_gau-links; this portion behaves like a Frobenius morphism / Teichmüller deformation and is responsible for 'volume distortion' which is the ultimate computational target (Remark 4.10.3 (ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or constructing links one must treat the value-group component as deformable; comparisons must account for the induced dilation/volume distortion rather than assuming invariance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility constraints: conjugate synchronization and F±_l-symmetries
rubrics_metrics.description: Within a Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater the construction requires conjugate synchronization (compatibility between copies of absolute Galois groups at l-torsion points) that is compatible with the F±_l-symmetry; both anabelian and post-anabelian representations of Gaussian monoids must be handled compatibly to construct the Θ×μ_gau-link and later apply log-wall techniques (Remarks 4.11.2 (ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical instruction: when producing the Gaussian-moniod-related structures, ensure the conjugate synchronization property holds and that representations used (anabelian or post-anabelian) are chosen appropriately depending on whether one is building the Θ×μ_gau-link or preparing for log-wall applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical splittings of Gaussian monoids into unit and value-group components
rubrics_metrics.description: At v ∈ Vbad, Gaussian monoids admit canonical splittings into 'unit' and 'value group' components; these splittings correspond to 'non-deformed' (coricity) and 'Teichmüller-dilated' (value-group) real dimensions respectively, and are crucial for later constructions (Remark 4.11.2 (ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assembling Gaussian distributions or monoids, the canonical splitting must be identified and used: it underlies multiradial formulations, conjugate synchronization, and is essential for log-wall applications.
